headline: High-risk shared cloud-workspace automation: Devin can write/egress broadly while dexter can exfiltrate financial data via APIs, creating medium leakage and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can read/write cloud workspace files and use MCP, Slack, GitHub, and browsers; dexter uses autonomous execution with files in .dexter/scratchpad and broad network egress. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent consumes the other's outputs from shared files or integrations. No direct shared channel is documented, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF Devin reads dexter-produced text from a shared workspace, Slack thread, or MCP payload as instructions.
IF dexter ingests Devin-generated repo or chat content without provenance checks.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and disable shared file mounts.
Require provenance tags on all inter-agent messages.
Route cross-agent content through a human review step.
Disable MCP channels not needed for the task.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens; dexter touches financial and market data and calls OpenAI and other external APIs. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive data can flow from Devin into dexter's outbound API calls. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace by default, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF both agents are given access to the same repo, scratchpad, or chat export.
IF dexter is allowed to send Devin-originated files or prompts to external APIs.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared folders.
Use separate API keys per agent.
Block outbound uploads from shared workspaces.
Redact tokens before handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin can modify git state, write the filesystem, and use broad network egress; dexter has autonomous execution and broad network egress. If both operate on the same repo or mutable workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state. The profiles do not mention locking or coordination, so the unsafe default is a high conflict risk.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git checkout or writable directory.
IF neither orchestrator provides file or branch locking.
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent.
Use read-only clones for one agent.
Serialize write phases with a lock file.
Limit one agent to network-only or write-only duties.
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency control around shared repos.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that can act on browser, shell, and integrations; dexter runs autonomously and can call external APIs. If dexter's outputs are treated as authoritative by Devin, errors can cascade into commits, tickets, or messages. The pair lacks a documented verification gate, but the downstream blast radius is not proven irreversible, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Devin uses dexter output as a source of truth for code, tickets, or messages.
IF no human or automated verification step checks dexter's claims before action.
mitigations: Require citations for all factual claims.
Add a verification checklist before actions.
Restrict Devin from auto-sending external messages.
Use dry-run mode for first pass.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs, while dexter handles financial and market data and sends data to external APIs. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if regulated financial data or sensitive internal data crosses between them. No specific jurisdiction or certification mismatch is documented, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is placed into Devin-managed chat, docs, or issue trackers.
IF dexter forwards that data to third-party APIs without a DPA or retention controls.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared prompts.
Review API retention settings.
Use region-restricted endpoints where available.
Document data-class boundaries per agent.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement.
